facts.text: On this date in 1863, Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address in roughly two minutes. The featured speaker that day, Edward Everett, had spoken for two hours before him.
On Nov 19, 1942, the Soviet counteroffensive at Stalingrad began — encircling 300,000 German troops in a turning point that cost more lives than the entire Pacific War.
Mongolia has a lower population density than any sovereign nation on Earth: about 2 people per square kilometer, yet its capital Ulaanbaatar holds nearly half the entire country's population.
More people live within a 4,000 km radius centered on Dhaka than live outside it — roughly half of all humanity fits inside a circle that excludes most of Europe and the Americas.
The city of Chongqing, China, administers an area larger than Austria and governs over 32 million people, making it arguably the largest city on Earth by both area and registered population.
On this day in 1929, three weeks after Black Tuesday, the Dow hit its post-crash dead-cat bounce peak — then fell another 86% over the next three years.
On Nov 19, 1954, the first Waffle House opened in Avondale Estates, Georgia. It never went public, is still family-controlled, and FEMA uses it as an informal disaster-recovery indicator.
The entire US junk bond market was essentially invented by one person: Michael Milken at Drexel Burnham Lambert financed more than 1,000 companies with high-yield debt in the 1980s.
Saudi Aramco paid out more in dividends in 2023 — roughly $98 billion — than Apple, Microsoft, and Google combined returned to shareholders that year.
The Dutch East India Company, often called the first publicly traded firm, was so dominant that at its peak its inflation-adjusted valuation exceeded $8 trillion — more than any company in history.

On this date in 1969, Apollo 12 landed on the Moon with such precision that astronauts walked to the Surveyor 3 probe 183 meters away — a robotic craft that had been sitting there for two and a half years.

On this date in 1932, Nobel laureate James Chadwick submitted his landmark paper confirming the neutron exists — a particle so shy it passed through lead walls that would stop any known radiation cold.
Your skeleton is not the rigid scaffold it appears. Bone is a living tissue that completely replaces itself roughly every decade, quietly remodeling under mechanical stress while you sleep.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
The human eye can detect a single photon — one quantum of light — under ideal dark-adapted conditions. Your brain suppresses this sensitivity during daylight so the world does not look like static.
On this day in 1863, Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address — a speech so short that the photographer never got a clean shot. The featured orator, Edward Everett, spoke for two hours before him.
On this day in 1969, Apollo 12 landed on the Moon. The mission's backup crew included a young Jack Swigert, who would later die as a sitting U.S. Congressman-elect before he could be sworn in.

The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 26 years before the transcontinental railroad was completed. You could theoretically fax a document before you could efficiently cross the continent to deliver it.
Oxford University began teaching students in 1096. The Aztec Empire didn't exist until 1428. Oxford is older than the Aztecs.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramid was built around 2560 BC.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast it blurs the line between invented word and real one.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Also Koenig's invention — proof that a single person can hand a name to a feeling millions already carried in silence.
On this day in 1863, Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address. The word 'dedicate' appears six times in 272 words — a rhetorical hammer the Latin 'dedicare', to consecrate, was built for.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word meaning the shared, wordless look between two people who both want something neither will initiate. Yaghan was once called the world's most succinct language.
On this day in 1942, Soviet forces launched Operation Uranus. The codename came from the Greek god Ouranos — 'sky' — a habit of naming offensives upward, as if altitude conferred victory.

On this date in 2017, Bitcoin crossed $8,000 for the first time — then doubled again within three weeks, reaching $19,783 by Dec 17, the fastest 10x move by a trillion-dollar asset class in recorded financial history.
On this date in 2013, the FBI auctioned 29,656 BTC seized from Silk Road. Winning bidder Tim Draper paid ~$632 each. Those coins would be worth over $2.9B at 2024 peaks.

Bitcoin's timelock opcode, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, was only activated in 2015 — six years after launch. The chain processed roughly 100 million transactions before it could natively lock funds to a future block.
Ethereum's gas limit is set by miners and validators, not the protocol. It has been raised over 20 times since 2015, meaning the chain's throughput ceiling is a social consensus, not a hard rule.

The smallest bitcoin denomination, 1 satoshi, equals 0.00000001 BTC. At Bitcoin's 2024 all-time high, one satoshi was worth approximately $0.00107 — more than some sovereign currencies' smallest units.

On this date in 2022, Stability AI released Stable Diffusion 2.0 — shifting the image generation landscape by open-sourcing weights that anyone could run locally, ending the era when such capability required API access.
On this date in 2019, OpenAI released the full GPT-2 model after a staged rollout it had delayed citing misuse concerns — a caution the field largely abandoned within two years.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins, roughly every catalogued organism on Earth, in a single 2022 release — compressing what biologists estimated as centuries of experimental work.
The training run for GPT-4 is estimated to have consumed around 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of roughly 4,500 average US households.
RLHF, the technique central to making LLMs follow instructions, was first described in a 2017 DeepMind paper on training Atari agents from human preferences — not originally a language idea at all.
